02 The examples

## What winning looks like

Six rounds, word for word. The words in orange give DeepL's version away; the words in green are what a local says.

An Argentine is broke sin un mango and gets paid when they cobran . El día de pago reads like a translation.

“ We're renting a small apartment with a pool. ”

In casual Mexican speech you rentas a depa with an alberca . DeepL's version is the textbook one.

“ My girlfriend is coming over for dinner tonight. ”

In Quebec your girlfriend is your blonde . Ma chum usually means a friend.

“ Give me a kilo of tomatoes and some bread. ”

In a Cairo market bread is عيش and you ask with هاتلي . DeepL writes formal Modern Standard Arabic.

“ I'll take a taxi to the subway station. ”

Taipei rides the 捷運 . 地鐵 is the mainland word.

“ It's freezing outside, wear a warm hat. ”

Quebec says il fait frette , and tuque is feminine. DeepL used an idiom from France and got the gender wrong, in a variant it offers by name.

03 DeepL's wins

## The scoreboard is honest

DeepL won 3 rounds, and they matter, because they show the judge will rule against us. All 3 were small calls on wording and rhythm.

“ Hand me my sweater, it's getting cold. ”

In Spain you hand someone el jersey , not mi jersey . A fair call.

“ My phone battery died, can I borrow a charger? ”

The judge preferred a bateria acabou to our ficou sem bateria , while calling both great.

“ I bought fresh pineapple at the market. ”

The judge wanted a 的 between 新鮮 and 鳳梨 for the rhythm of everyday speech.

04 Availability

## A continent is not a country

DeepL's answer to Latin America is one Spanish for the whole region, and it has one Arabic, written in the formal style. Egypt and Saudi Arabia, whose street speech splits in the first three words of a price haggle, finished 10 to 0 and 10 to 0. AIR Translate offers Spanish for 23 countries and Arabic for 23 , because Buenos Aires is not Mexico City and Cairo is not Riyadh.

05 Method

## How the test works

- 1 118 52 sentences, 11 countries Everyday English, written so that a natural rendering differs by country in vocabulary, idiom, register or script. Sibling variants share the same sentences: 118 rounds in all.

52 sentences, 11 countries

Everyday English, written so that a natural rendering differs by country in vocabulary, idiom, register or script. Sibling variants share the same sentences: 118 rounds in all.

- 2 ES-419 DeepL at its strongest Latin American Spanish for every Latin American variant, Quebec French for Quebec, both Portuguese variants natively, Traditional Chinese for Taiwan, and less formal wording to match the casual sentences.

DeepL at its strongest

Latin American Spanish for every Latin American variant, Quebec French for Quebec, both Portuguese variants natively, Traditional Chinese for Taiwan, and less formal wording to match the casual sentences.

- 3 A / B A blind referee from Google Gemini 4 Argon , at its default settings, saw the two answers as A and B and was asked which a native of that country would find natural. If it leans toward anyone, it is not us.
